summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (N13) proposing an assay to test whether methylene blue (MB) under concurrent dual selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) + MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) matches MB-alone rescue on a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay. The document is a research-stage hypothesis/assay proposal with a negative status label, meaning the key experimental comparison (MB-under-dual vs MB-alone on COX-amnestic assay) has not been run. It synthesizes prior literature to frame the mechanistic question of whether MB's memory-rescue effect is MAO-driven or redox/COX-driven.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, MB under concurrent dual selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) + selective MAO-B inhibitor (selegiline/rasagiline-class) matches MB-alone rescue — retention Δ >70% of MB-alone (or inside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). This is a PREDICTION; the experiment has NOT been run.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: The core mechanistic question is redox-vs-MAO for MB's memory rescue on the COX-amnestic/metabolic-memory class. MB restores retention after COX inhibition and is a preferential reversible MAO-A inhibitor. Selective MAO-A (clorgyline-class) and MAO-B (rasagiline/selegiline-class) tools exist, but no published MB-under-dual COX-amnestic retention head-to-head (H2H) vs MB-alone exists. N12 (dual-alone failure) left open the occupancy-subtraction escape: concurrent dual MAOI could still subtract MB rescue. N13 is designed to close that escape using the same assay with an MB-alone positive-control arm. Competing caveat: underperformance of MB+dual vs MB-alone could reflect off-target/PK interaction rather than MAO occupancy.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Baseline
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature references are cited:
1. PMID 12384216 (DOI 10.1016/s0304-3940(02)00827-3) — Callaway/Gonzalez-Lima: low-dose MB restores spatial memory retention impaired by a cytochrome oxidase inhibitor. No MB-under-dual selective MAOI arm.
2. PMID 21087672 (DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.11.023; PMC3026638) — MB beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (metabolic/network framing). No MB-under-dual selective MAOI arm.
3. PMID 17721552 (DOI 10.1038/sj.bjp.0707430; PMC2078225) — Ramsay 2007: MB potent reversible preferential MAO-A inhibition (serotonin-toxicity prediction). Enzyme/isoform prior, not MB-under-dual COX-amnestic H2H.
4. PMID 26142126 (DOI 10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2015.05.009) — Weinreb 2015: rasagiline (selective MAO-B-i) improves cognitive deficits and related cascades in aged mice. MAO-B tool prior, not MB-under-dual COX-amnestic retention vs MB-alone.

content_blocks.title: Relationship to Prior Cards (N5–N12)
content_blocks.content: N13 is explicitly distinct from prior cards: N12 (dual-alone failure, left occupancy-subtraction escape open), N10/N11 (single arms, never co-dosed MB under MAOI), N5 (MAO-A generic working memory, A-biased), N8 (Azure B metabolite arm), N9 (redox-dead arm). None of N5–N12 ran MB-under-dual selective MAOI on the COX-amnestic assay. Soft-complete for MB∩dual selective MAOI∩COX-amnestic = 0.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Caveats
content_blocks.content:
1. N5–N12 do not prove N13: N12 dual-alone failure ≠ MB-under-dual preservation; N10/N11 single arms never co-dosed MB under MAOI; N5 was A-biased/generic WM; N8/N9 ran metabolite/redox-dead arms; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated MB-under-dual match on COX-amnestic.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue PD: Ramsay is preferential MAO-A enzyme inhibition; Weinreb 26142126 is aged-cognition/cascades; clorgyline 26825854 is monoamine/affective HD — none is MB + dual selective MAOI on COX-amnestic retention vs MB-alone.
3. Occupancy-subtraction escape + occupancy matching: do not collapse N12 into MB-under-dual proof; underperformance of MB+dual vs MB-alone could be PK/off-target rather than MAO occupancy; assay MAO-A/B occupancy/monoamine readout without a dosing card; use same COX-inhibitor amnestic class where parent MB restores, with MB-alone as positive control. No dosing invented.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Method and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Method: propose-assay (NOT_RUN). Refutation criterion: On the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, MB under concurrent dual selective MAO-A-i + MAO-B-i fails to match MB-alone (retention Δ ≤70% of MB-alone or outside the MB-equivalence band) — especially under exposure/MAO-A/B-occupancy-matched conditions — so MAO-occupancy necessity for MB metabolic-memory rescue survives and redox-only framing fails. Ablation analysis identifies three critical design elements: (1) behavioral H2H on Gonzalez-Lima class assay with MB-alone arm, (2) concurrent dual selective MAO-A + MAO-B identity co-dosed with parent MB, (3) N5–N12≠proof discipline.

content_blocks.title: Execution and IP Status
content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Kill cost tier: 1 (cheap). Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. The assay is proposed but has not been conducted. No dosing card exists. No observed quantitative results are available.

key_findings: Experiment N13 has NOT been run (execution_status=NOT_RUN); all quantitative outcomes are PREDICTIONS, not observed data.

The key experimental gap: no published or internal study has tested MB under concurrent dual selective MAO-A-i (clorgyline-class) + MAO-B-i (selegiline/rasagiline-class) vs MB-alone on a COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay (soft-complete = 0).
Literature confirms MB restores spatial memory retention after COX inhibition (PMID 12384216) and has beneficial network effects in amnestic models (PMID 21087672).
MB is a potent reversible preferential MAO-A inhibitor (PMID 17721552, Ramsay 2007), creating the mechanistic ambiguity: is MB's memory rescue MAO-driven or redox/COX-driven?
Rasagiline is validated as a selective MAO-B tool with cognitive effects in aged mice (PMID 26142126, Weinreb 2015).
N12 (dual-alone failure) left the occupancy-subtraction escape open — N13 is designed to close it by co-dosing MB with dual MAOI and comparing to MB-alone.
Predicted threshold: MB+dual retention Δ >70% of MB-alone (or inside pre-registered MB-equivalence band) would support redox/COX framing over MAO-occupancy framing.
